newsitem.title: USA: W African crude steals spotlight on US Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: W African crude steals spotlight on US Gulf Coast.

text.p: West African crude stole the spotlight among foreign crudes along the U.S. Gulf Coast on Wednesday, traders said.
Traders said earlier weakness in West African crude prices had prompted a seller to deliver Nigerian Bonny Light crude into NYMEX.

The talk was fueled by the current premium for wet barrels of West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, as traders holding paper positions struggle to avoid the uncertainty of receiving a crude other than WTI when the May contract expires next Tuesday, traders said.
Elsewhere in the region, Nigerian Forcados was looking for a home after several were placed on Tuesday around West Texas Intermediate/Cushing minus $1.00 a barrel for the last decade of May.
Angolan Palanca changed hands at WTI minus 75 cents a barrel, traders said.
From the North Sea, Norwegian Oseberg was on offer at WTI minus 75-80 cents a barrel for mid-May arrival.
In Latin America, Chile's state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) is seeking to buy 960,000 barrels of crude oil for delivery at the end of May to early June, trade sources said.
The tender will be awarded on April 17.
In its last purchase tender, ENAP bought 360,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente crude for delivery around May 20.
Separately, Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol is receiving bids today to sell a cargo of Cano Limon crude for loading at the end of May, trade sources said.
Meanhwile, Ecuadoran Oriente to the U.S. West Coast was heard offered at Alaska North Slope minus $1.50-35 a barrel.
